question: A team records every decision it makes only inside chat messages, spread across many separate conversations. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The decisions will be phrased inconsistently, which makes the team's writing style vary a lot.
B) The conversations will each reach their length limit, forcing the team to start new ones often.
C) There is no single current version, so different people act on different versions of a decision.
D) The team will spend more of its usage allowance rereading conversations than it saves by chatting.
correct_answers: C) There is no single current version, so different people act on different versions of a decision.
explanations: Incorrect. Inconsistent phrasing is cosmetic next to colleagues acting on conflicting versions of the same decision.
Incorrect. Restarting conversations is an inconvenience rather than the substantive problem with keeping decisions only in chat.
Correct. Decisions scattered across conversations have no canonical home, so colleagues find whichever message they find and proceed on out-of-date or superseded information.
Incorrect. Rereading a conversation is cheap, and cost is not what makes scattered decisions dangerous.
